On load, `AuthLoader` (from `react-query-auth`, configured in `src/lib/auth.tsx`) calls `getUser`, which requests `/auth/me` through the shared Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. `AuthLoader` is mounted in `src/app/provider.tsx` and shows a spinner until that request settles. The result is cached as the user query, and `useUser()` reads it everywhere else. `ProtectedRoute` in `src/lib/auth.tsx`, used around the `/app` routes in `src/app/router.tsx`, sends the user to `/auth/login?redirectTo=...` when there is no user data. `src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx` does the reverse on the sign-in and registration pages: once a user is loaded, it navigates to `redirectTo` or the dashboard.

Every request goes through the response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. For any error it shows an error toast with the server's message, then, if the status is 401, it sets `window.location.href` to the login page with a `redirectTo` value. Because the interceptor also handles `/auth/me`, a signed-out visitor gets a toast and a hard redirect on load. The promise is still rejected, so `ProtectedRoute` also redirects if the failure was not a 401.

The 401 redirect has a bug. The code creates an empty `new URLSearchParams()` and reads `redirectTo` from it, so the value is always null and the fallback `window.location.pathname` is always used. The query string is dropped, so a user sent to sign-in from `/app/discussions?page=2` comes back to `/app/discussions`, which contradicts the rule that sign-in returns people to the page they wanted. There is a second risk I did not run: if `/auth/me` returns 401 while the user is already on `/auth/login`, the interceptor would navigate to the same login URL again, which could reload in a loop. I only read the code and did not reproduce it in a browser. Separately, the mock `/auth/me` handler in `src/testing/mocks/handlers/auth.ts` returns 500 for a signed-out user rather than 401, so local development never exercises the 401 path on load.
